explanation: Parchment (surface), Quill (tool), Inkwell (supply), and Scribe (person) are all elements central to the historical, hand-written production of documents before the Industrial Revolution. A Typewriter is a mechanical device invented much later.

Gargoyles, Flying Buttresses, Rose Windows, and Pointed Arches are all distinctive features of Gothic architecture. A Pediment, however, is a triangular gable typically found in Classical Greek and Roman architecture.
Bark, Roar, Hiss, and Chirp are all verbs used to describe specific sounds made by animals. Gallop describes a way an animal moves, not a sound it produces.
